title: Introduction to cori.data.bfs
text: data returned long format: one row per geoid / year / variable. Filter specific geographies, years, variables:
code: df <- get_business_applications(geography = "county")  dplyr::glimpse(df) # New Hampshire counties, 2010 onward nh_bfs <- get_business_applications(   geoids = grep("^33", unique(df$geoid), value = TRUE),   years  = 2010:2024 )  dplyr::glimpse(nh_bfs)

title: Introduction to cori.data.bfs
text: Business formation diverges rural nonrural counties. chart shows total business applications rural status using CBSA 2023 rural definition.
code: library(cori.charts) library(ggplot2) library(ruraldefinitions) library(dplyr)  load_fonts()  rural_xwalk <- ruraldefinitions::cbsa_2023 |>   select(geoid, is_rural)  rural_avg <- df |>   left_join(rural_xwalk, by = "geoid") |>   filter(!is.na(is_rural)) |>   group_by(year, is_rural) |>   summarise(value = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")  ggplot(rural_avg, aes(x = year, y = value, color = is_rural)) +   annotate("rect", xmin = 2007.9, xmax = 2009.5,            ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4) +   annotate("rect", xmin = 2020, xmax = 2020.5,            ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.4) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(size = 2.5) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("Rural" = "#2F6E9B", "Nonrural" = "#7EBDC2"),     labels = c("Rural" = "Rural counties", "Nonrural" = "Nonrural counties")   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = seq(2005, 2024, by = 4),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))   ) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "K")) +   theme_cori() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   labs(     title    = "Rural business formation surged during the pandemic and has held",     subtitle = "Total business applications (BA series), 2005\u20132024",     x        = NULL,     y        = NULL,     color    = NULL,     caption  = paste0(       "Source: CORI analysis of U.S. Census Bureau Business Formation Statistics.\n",       "Shaded bands mark Great Recession (2008\u201309) and COVID-19 (2020). ",       "Rural classification: CORI CBSA 2023 definition."     )   )

 variables = "population",   years     = 2005:2024 ) |>   select(geoid, year, population = value)  grafton <- grafton_bfs |>   left_join(grafton_pop, by = c("geoid", "year")) |>   mutate( text: data frame columns: variable, raw_variable, label, unit, notes. raw_variable original name stored S3 parquet files.

title: Get the cori.data.bfs variable codebook — get_bfs_codebook
code: get_bfs_codebook() #>                variable          raw_variable                 label #> 1 business_applications business_applications Business applications #>           unit #> 1 applications #>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    notes #> 1 Total business applications (BA series). Counts EIN applications filed with the IRS, excluding tax liens, estates, trusts, agriculture (NAICS 11), and public administration (NAICS 92). County, state, and national coverage. Coverage: 2005-present.

title: Get Business Formation Statistics — get_business_applications
text: Queries CORI's processed Business Formation Statistics (BFS) parquet files S3 using DuckDB. Returns long-format data: one row per geoid / year / variable.

title: Get Business Formation Statistics — get_business_applications
code: get_business_applications(   geography = c("all", "county", "state", "nation"),   years = NULL,   geoids = NULL,   variables = NULL,   vintage = "latest" )

title: Get Business Formation Statistics — get_business_applications
text: geography Character. One "", "county", "state", "nation". Filters rows geography level. Default: "". years Integer vector. Years return. Default: available. geoids Character vector. FIPS codes return (5-digit county, 2-digit state, "00" national). supplied, overrides geography. Default: . variables Character vector. Variables return. Default: . See get_bfs_codebook() valid names. vintage Character. Vintage read, e.g. "2024". Default: "latest", reads _LATEST pointer written write_bfs_processed_to_s3().

title: Get Business Formation Statistics — get_business_applications
text: data frame columns: geoid, year, variable, value.

what: Write processed BFS data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_bfs_processed_to_s3
title: Write processed BFS data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_bfs_processed_to_s3
text: Downloads Census BFS Excel file, processes four-column tidy format, writes year-partitioned parquet files S3. _LATEST pointer file updated get_business_applications() can find current vintage.

title: Write processed BFS data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_bfs_processed_to_s3
code: write_bfs_processed_to_s3(   years = 2005:as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),   s3_bucket = "cori.data.bfs",   s3_path_prefix = "",   overwrite = FALSE,   sync_to_s3 = TRUE )

title: Write processed BFS data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_bfs_processed_to_s3
text: years Integer vector. Years include. Default: 2005 current year. s3_bucket Character. S3 bucket name. Default: "cori.data.bfs". s3_path_prefix Character. Optional prefix S3 keys, e.g. "test/" development. Default: "". overwrite Logical. TRUE, delete existing S3 vintage prefix uploading. Default: FALSE. sync_to_s3 Logical. Upload S3 writing locally. Default: TRUE.

title: Write processed BFS data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_bfs_processed_to_s3
text: Invisibly, named list: $vintage $n_rows.
